tools.name: get_scene
tools.title: Get scene
tools.description: Returns the full scene graph: flat node dictionary, root node IDs, collections, and explicit installed plugin IDs when present.

tools.name: validate_design
tools.title: Validate design
tools.description: Check a design (procedural item recipe) without changing the scene. Returns `valid`, coded `diagnostics` with paths (errors block placement, warnings flag floating or unbalanced parts), the parameter `sweep`, and `measurements` at the given parameters: bounds, per-part bounds and instances, true triangle counts, draw groups per slot, datum contact and connected components. It is the authority: some rules are not expressible in pascal://schema/design. Repair and re-validate until `valid` is true. Version 2 designs validate fully but carry a design_version_not_enabled warning: placement accepts version 1 only until the next release.

design.description: The design (procedural recipe, version 1 or 2) as an object, or as a JSON string for clients that cannot send recursive objects. Schema: pascal://schema/design.

parameters.description: Parameter values to measure at, by parameter id. Defaults otherwise.

tools.name: place_design
tools.title: Place design
tools.description: Create one instance of a design (procedural item recipe, object or JSON string) in the scene. The design must pass validate_design. Its mounting picks the host: floor designs go on a level (or a slab or zone of it) or on a named surface of a placed design; wall-side designs on a straight wall face; ceiling designs under a ceiling. Only creates: refusals carry a code (invalid_design with diagnostics, design_version_not_enabled for version 2 designs until the next release, design_too_large above 24 KiB, invalid_placement, node_exists, host_not_found, wrong_host, unknown_surface, does_not_fit) and change nothing.

design.description: The design (procedural recipe, version 1 or 2) as an object, or as a JSON string for clients that cannot send recursive objects. Schema: pascal://schema/design.

hostId.description: Floor designs: a level, or a slab or zone on it, or a placed design with surfaceId. Wall-side designs: a straight wall. Ceiling designs: a ceiling.

position.description: Metres. Floor: level-local [x, y, z], y above the floor. Wall-side: [along, height, offset] of the mounting reference from the wall start. Ceiling: plan [x, 0, z] of the reference. Surface: [x, 0, z] in the surface frame.

rotation.description: Yaw. Not for wall-side designs; use side to face the other way. In radians, or text with a unit ("90°").

side.description: Wall face for wall-side designs: front is the +normal side, normal (−Δz, Δx) of start→end. The wall's frontSide and backSide say which face is exterior (a facade light goes on that one).

surfaceId.description: Named surface of the host design to rest on (see validate_design measurements.surfaces).

parameters.description: Parameter values to measure at, by parameter id. Defaults otherwise.

slots.description: Slot id to "#rrggbb" or a scene:/library: material reference.

id.description: Optional new id ("procedural-item_…"). Refused if it exists: this tool only creates.

tools.name: measure_stair
tools.title: Measure stair
tools.description: Inspect actual flight risers, walking-line going, slope, arrival, uniformity, headroom against floors, ceilings and stair bodies, and design-target diagnostics without changing measured geometry.

available.description: The space a new layout may take, to propose layouts that fit it.

width.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

length.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

tools.name: fit_stair
tools.title: Fit stair
tools.description: Explicitly replace stair riser proportions with uniform risers from design targets. Optionally fit going by changing flight runs or arc sweep; preserves landing elevations. Optional straight, L or U layout replaces the flight chain with width-sized turning landings or quarter-turn winders. Winder going is measured along the selected walking line. One atomic edit.

width.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

landingDepth.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

innerGap.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

walkingLineOffset.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

maxRiserHeight.description: The tallest riser (default 0.18 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

minimumGoing.description: The shortest going (default 0.25 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

targetGoing.description: The going a fit aims for (default 0.28 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

minimumHeadroom.description: The least headroom over the flight (default 2 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

tools.name: find_by_type
tools.title: Find by type
tools.description: Find everything of one type in the scene, wherever it lives: nodes of that kind (column, door, window, wall, stair, imported-mesh, a plugin's kind…), items of that category, lights (any item that emits light), and typed parts inside scripted objects, windows and doors (a porch's columns, a window's grille). Narrow it to a level, a parent, a zone or an importer's source ids; without a type, every node the other filters match. A word that names nothing (no node kind, nor an item category or part type in this scene) is refused with the kinds the scene holds. Each result gives the node's id, name, kind, level and parent, with its metadata and provenance when it has them (one over 1 KB is named in omitted instead); get_node reads a node whole. Parts are read-only: they come back with their object's id, the part id and, for objects directly on a level, its bounds in level coordinates; edit them through their object. count says how many match; past limit (200 unless asked) the rest are left out of results, with truncated: narrow the call or raise limit.

type.description: What to find, one word: a node kind (wall, slab, imported-mesh, fixture:bench), an item category, light, or a part type (column, beam, panel, railing, trim…). Omit it to find every node the other filters match.

levelId.description: Only this level. Default: every level.

parentId.description: Only the nodes directly under this one: a wall's doors and windows, a roof's segments, a level's walls.

zoneId.description: Only what stands in this zone: on the zone's level, its plan point inside the zone's outline and outside its holes (a wall's midpoint, a polygon's centroid, a door or window where its wall puts it, a block or mesh by the middle of its geometry, a part with bounds by their middle).

sourceId.description: Only the nodes an importer recorded under this source id (provenance.refs[].id, or legacy metadata.sourceIds), exactly. Characters outside printable ASCII also match their percent-encoded form.

sourceIdPrefix.description: Only the nodes with a source id starting with this.

limit.description: How many results to list at most. Default 200; count still says how many match.

tools.name: list_levels
tools.title: List levels
tools.description: List every level of every building in floor order: id, name, floorIndex, building (parentId), role (occupied storey, roof-only level or support level), child count, gradeStanding (at-grade, partly-below-grade or below-grade against the ground line and the terrain), isGroundLevel, and which one the person is viewing (isActive); groundLevels names, per building, the level at grade (levelId, whether the building names it, floorElevation, gradeElevation, floorOverGrade, seated). A roof-only level is the roof, not a storey.

tools.name: get_node
tools.title: Get node
tools.description: Get the full data of any node by its id: its fields as stored, with what the scene decides for it beside them (a wall's or a ceiling's resolvedHeight, and heightIsExplicit, false when it follows its storey; a wall's resolvedThickness; a door's or window's resolvedOpening, its floor and what it hangs from; the displayName a level or a floor plate is shown by); its ancestorIds, its parent first (a door's wall, then the level, the building, the site); and the scene materials (scene:<id>) its finishes use. A container's node lists its children as stored; any that name no node are listed again in missingChildIds. A node its schema rejects comes back as stored, with nothing derived (verify_scene says what is wrong).

tools.name: get_level_summary
tools.title: Get level summary
tools.description: Summarise one level so nothing on it goes unseen: its role and counts, then walls (length, heights, doors and windows), zones (name, area, size, floor_choices), slabs, ceilings, items (floor, wall and ceiling), floor openings, stairs, roofs, and anything else by type. Zone polygons: get_zones; a node's full data: get_node.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

tools.name: get_walls
tools.title: Get walls
tools.description: Get the walls of a level: start and end in metres, length, stored and resolved height, thickness, and their doors and windows. wallFaceChains gives base-chain provenance for geometric faces a (left of start → end) and b (right): ref (authored face slot), legacy (inline spec), or default (declared fallback ref). These are not final rendered finishes: room intent, face paint regions, exterior assembly cladding and reference availability can change appearance. A chosen white or default-matching ref is legitimate; fallback alone is not a defect or a requirement to paint.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

tools.name: get_zones
tools.title: Get zones
tools.description: Get the zones (rooms) of a level: name, colour, polygon and holes in metres, area in m² (holes taken out), bounding size, and floor_choices: the floor plates the room can take (key, plateId, name, current; drawn and mezzanine flags). A room shares its floor plate with the rooms next to it unless detached. Persisted authored wall intent is wallMaterial (string, or null when absent) and wallOverrides (records of wallId, geometric face a or b, and finish; [] when absent). This is not a final rendered finish or visual verification: local overrides and face paint can take precedence, and absent room intent is not a defect or a requirement to paint.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

tools.name: duplicate_level
tools.title: Duplicate level
tools.description: Copy a level with everything on it, as the editor does: fresh ids, internal links kept, and units whose rooms are all on that level copied too; plan references, scans and spawn points stay behind. The copy goes above the original (or below it) and the floors past it move up one.

levelId.description: The level to copy, by an id list_levels returned. Default: the floor the person is viewing.

position.description: Where the copy goes: above the original (default) or below it.

name.description: Name of the copy. Default: none, so it reads by its floor like a new level (Floor 1, Ground floor…).

preset.description: What to copy, as in the editor: everything (default); structure (walls, zones, slabs, ceilings, roofs, stairs, doors, windows) without materials; structure with its materials; or structure and furniture.

tools.name: set_ground_level
tools.title: Set ground level
tools.description: Make a level the building's ground floor: the one standing at grade, its floor 8 in over the ground (about 6 in on cast concrete foundations, 12 in on stone: the building's foundation construction seats it; the result names it). A building's levels stack on a ground line; the levels with a lower floor index are below grade (basements), the ones at or over it are not, and list_levels reads it as groundLevels (levelId, floorElevation, floorOverGrade, seated) and each level's gradeStanding (at-grade, partly-below-grade, below-grade) and isGroundLevel. This names the level on the building, seats the building so that level's floor datum, the top of the foundation where the wood framing starts, stands 0.203 m (8 in) over grade on a block foundation, 0.15 m on cast concrete (Europe), 0.3 m on stone (a historic style) (flat site: world Y 0.203; sculpted terrain: 0.203 m over the mean ground height under its floor), moving the building in height only — the plan stays where it is and every level keeps its place relative to the others — and renumbers the floor indices so it is 0 and the ones under it are -1, -2…. A level added below (add_level position below) stacks under the lowest level without moving the ground floor. A roof level or a support level cannot be the ground floor (not_a_storey). One undo step. Refusals: level_not_found, not_a_level, no_building, not_a_storey. Answering unchanged: true when the level is already the named ground floor, at that seat, at index 0.

levelId.description: The level to stand at grade, by an id list_levels returned.

tools.name: verify_scene
tools.title: Verify scene
tools.description: Optional whole-scene evidence: per-level content, roles (storey, roof-only, support) and the spaces its walls enclose, then every problem found, each with a type: empty levels, walls with no room or door, a space the walls enclose with no room over it (space_no_room) or with several and no wall between them (space_many_rooms), a room the walls do not close (room_not_enclosed) or with no name (room_unnamed), rooms with no floor or ceiling, storeys with no stair, roof levels misused, walls intersecting a covering slab or ending coplanar with its walking surface (wall_covering_slab_contact, with wallId and slabId), openings off their wall, stairs off their slab or blocked, furniture blocking a door or overlapping, a house past its lot line or in its required yards, every node field its schema rejects (schema_invalid, with its nodeId and path; valid is then false, and the level holding the node lists it as unread and is measured once it is fixed), a node kind no schema here knows, once per kind (schema_unknown_kind, info: a plugin kind), a hidden site (site_hidden). Static authored ceiling objects report transformed bounds extending above their ceiling attachment and bounds overlapping solid covering slab bands, with node IDs and measured metres; stored and derived slab holes are subtracted. Wall-mounted objects report a front oriented toward their host; static authored wall bounds report wall-body overlap and extension through the opposite face. With settled editor meshes, catalog wall bounds and large competing coplanar faces against the host or another item on the same wall are also measured within 1 mm. Hidden back-to-wall contact is not competing face evidence. These are observations, not instructions to change the scene or proof of exact mesh intersection. Bounds are measured in the owning building frame, including stacked level elevations. Unknown catalog raw bounds without meshes, animated models, unsupported attachment frames, unresolved scripted wall cuts, roof collisions, recessed slab shells and foundation volumes are not assessed.

tools.name: set_checkpoint
tools.title: Set a checkpoint
tools.description: A named moment in your work (a roof, a floor, a batch of walls) that verify_scene({ since: name }) can compare against: it lists what was created, changed and deleted since, grouped by level and kind with a view each, and what you made that is gone. "start", the beginning of your work, is always one; a name used again replaces the first; a session keeps at most 8. A checkpoint is kept with your session, not in the project: it changes nothing in the scene, enters no undo, and does not restore anything. Refused: too_many_checkpoints (naming them), scene_too_large, name_required.

name.description: A short name for this moment, e.g. "walls done" or "before roof".

tools.name: design_brief
tools.title: Write the design brief
tools.description:
The design brief of the request, written once for the whole request (piece by piece when the request invites it): the request read axis by axis (action, size, pieces, openings, style, materials, source, dressing), each axis bounded by the person's own words or open with a design statement, a vision, and where the objects come from. It is recorded as the design record of the turn and answers with what it unlocks. It changes nothing in the scene.
Furnishings are placed or made after a brief: place_items, furnish_room, place_in_room (the catalog's) and add_object, place_design (the agent's own), also inside run_batch. Before one, search_assets and view_assets read the catalog and every other tool works as usual; rooms, walls, openings and finishes are not furnishings.
Bounded and open, in four readings. "a 4 by 5 m bedroom with a double bed, two nightstands, a wardrobe, one window, one door": action, size, pieces (as a minimum: those pieces must be there, more may come) and openings bounded; style, materials, source and dressing open. "add a lamp next to the sofa": action and dressing bounded by "add a lamp" (one object in a room that exists); style open, its design statement saying how this lamp is designed. "a bedroom with only a bed and a lamp": pieces exact and dressing bounded by "only a bed and a lamp"; style and materials open, the bed and the lamp designed, not defaulted. "Build a house": the action bounded only by "a house"; every other axis open, the dressing included.
source open: the pieces are made (add_object, place_design), view_assets shows the catalog's pieces for reference, and furnish_room, which places a whole stock set, stays closed. asIs keeps technical equipment only (sanitaryware, kitchen and laundry appliances, heating and similar services): each piece is named with a reason and was shown by view_assets earlier in the same turn (chat) or session (MCP); furniture is made, not kept as it is. source catalog, brand or existing: place_items, furnish_room and place_in_room are open, and the creation tools stay open for what the catalog lacks.
Naming a piece (a double bed) states its function; its form, size within reason and finish are open unless the request fixes them. The pieces a request names are what the room must contain, not all it may contain: where the dressing axis is open, beyond states that design layer by layer: textiles, light, windows, walls, floor, plants, objects, small furniture, each a list of pieces or { none: why }, at least 6 of the 8 layers naming pieces; where the dressing is bounded (words that limit the pieces or the action, such as "only", "nothing else", "just"), none in every layer is accepted. The pieces the request names, read as a minimum, do not bound the dressing. The answer hands the pieces back as dressing.
A source other than open is set by the request, not chosen: sourceQuote holds the person's own words that name it, at least two words naming a brand (the brief's brand), the catalog or what is already there ("IKEA furniture only", "que du catalogue", "use my existing furniture"); a request that names no source is open. The chat checks the quote against the person's message of the turn, as it checks every bounded axis's quote; over MCP, where there is no message, a source quote must still name the source and is not compared with a request, and an axis quote is not compared either.
In the chat a brief lasts for the turn; over MCP it lasts for the session. The next design_brief replaces it. Refused: axis_missing (an axis is absent), axis_quote_not_in_request (a bounded axis's quote is not in the person's message), axis_open_without_design (an open axis without a design statement of at least 3 words), dressing_bounded_by_minimum (the dressing bounded by words inside a pieces quote read as a minimum), brand_required (source brand without a brand name), source_quote_required (a source other than open without sourceQuote), source_not_named (the quote names no brand, catalog or existing source), source_not_in_request (the quote is not in the person's message), beyond_too_thin (dressing open, fewer than 6 layers naming pieces).

tools.name: add_wall
tools.title: Add wall
tools.description: Add a single wall between two points on a level, straight or, with curveOffset, an arc. Refused with a code: a level that is not a storey (a declared roof level), and a wall shorter than 1 cm. On a level below grade, a wall against the ground (on the outline of the walls of the level) is a foundation wall, built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read; a partition inside the outline is an ordinary wall; the result says which.

start.description: [x, z] start point in level coordinates (metres).

end.description: [x, z] end point in level coordinates (metres).

thickness.description: Wall thickness (default 0.1 m; a wall against the ground on a level below grade, given none, is a foundation wall built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read; a partition inside it is an ordinary wall). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Wall height (default: the storey's height). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

curveOffset.description: Bends the wall into an arc: the sagitta, from the middle of the straight line start→end to the middle of the arc. Positive bows the middle toward the back face (the −normal side, normal (−Δz, Δx) of start→end), the arc's centre on the front side; negative the other way. At most half the chord (a half circle); more is clamped. A quarter round of radius r at a corner: end both walls r short of the corner and join their ends with an arc of curveOffset ±0.293·r, the sign that bows it outward. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

tools.name: add_fence
tools.title: Add fence
tools.description: Add a fence along points on a level: one fence per side, a whole run or a lot's boundary (closed) in one call. Privacy (solid panels) by default; picket for a picket fence, slat for vertical slats, rail for open rails, horizontal for cladding boards, guard for a deck's barrier. Fences stand on the level, as the editor's fence tool puts them. Refused with a code: a side shorter than 10 cm (fence_too_short), a roof level (roof_level).

points.description: [x, z] points in level coordinates (metres), the fence running through them in order.

closed.description: Close the run back to the first point, as a lot's boundary.

height.description: Fence height (default 1.8 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

style.description: slat | rail | privacy | horizontal | guard | picket (default privacy).

baseStyle.description: grounded (default: a kickboard on the ground), floating (the panel held off the ground on its posts) or raised (a bottom rail held above the ground, the posts to the ground: a deck guard).

materialPreset.description: A library material (library:<id>), found with search_materials.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

tools.name: add_corner_window
tools.title: Add corner window
tools.description: A window that wraps the corner where two walls meet: one window on each wall, both running to the corner and joined, the glass fused at the corner (post none, a fixed window's default) or meeting at a thin post (post post). Any angle the walls make, a bay's 135° as well as a square or an acute corner. The corner is the point the two walls end at ([x, z], as get_walls gives their ends); width is how far the glass runs along each wall from the corner, the same on both unless widths names a wall. Each side is placed by add_window's rules (height, sillHeight, windowType, style the same on both sides; with no sillHeight, centred on the lower of the two walls). The walls are the level's (levelId, default the floor the person is viewing): stacked storeys share their corners' points. Refused with a code: no_corner where no two walls of the level end at the point, corner_ambiguous where more than two do (name two with wallIds), corner_angle for a corner nearly folded back or nearly straight, corner_not_fused for post none on a window type other than fixed, width_exceeds_wall. Returns windowIds and wallIds; the editor's window panel shows the pair under Corner.

corner.description: The point where the two walls meet, [x, z] in the level's plan (m).

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

wallIds.description: The two walls, when more than two end at the corner.

width.description: How far the glass runs along each wall from the corner (default 1.2 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

widths.description: A width for a wall by its id, over width (e.g. { "wall_a": 1.6 }).

additionalProperties.description: The side on that wall. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Window height (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillHeight.description: Height from the floor to the bottom of the window (default: centred vertically on the lower of the two walls, the same on both sides). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

post.description: none: the glass fused at the corner (a fixed window's default); post: the glass meets at a thin post (the default, and the only choice, for the other window types, whose frames stay).

windowType.description: How it opens (default fixed), the window panel's Type row; the fused corner is a fixed window's.

style.description: The panes' look on each side (rows and columns), the window panel's Style row.

tools.name: merge_windows
tools.title: Merge windows
tools.description: Make two windows that exist one window, as the editor's Merge windows does: nothing is recreated. On two walls that meet at a corner, each window within 0.30 m of that corner, they become one corner window (the add_corner_window result): each is slid to the corner keeping its width, the glass fused (post none), and both take the first window's height, sill and type, so name first the window whose look you want; the corner is refused over 170° or under 10° (walls_not_meeting, corner_angle, window_not_at_corner, height_exceeds_wall). On one wall, two windows with at most 0.30 m between them and nothing between become one window spanning both outer edges, from the lower sill to the higher head, with the first window's type and style (windows_not_adjacent, opening_between). Refused with a code and a sentence that says why: window_not_found, not_a_window, same_window, window_not_on_wall, window_already_joined (unwrap it first), windows_already_joined, opening_overlap (sliding to the corner would land on another opening). Returns kind (corner or same_wall), the windows that stay (windowIds) and the one that went (removedIds). Use it for two windows already built that open a corner or one wide opening; add_corner_window builds a new pair, and verify_scene's corner_unjoined names two windows this joins.

windowIds.description: The two windows, the one whose height, sill and type the result keeps named first.

tools.name: add_level
tools.title: Add level
tools.description: Add an empty level to a building, as the editor does: above its top storey, under the building's roof level, which moves up one so the roof stays on top; or below its lowest level for a basement, which goes one storey under the lowest level and every existing level keeps its place, the ground floor included. On a scene with no building (a new or cleared scene), it starts the scene as the editor does: a site, a building and its ground level. A level that ends up below grade says in its result how a new wall on it is built (wallConstruction): a wall against the ground is a foundation wall, built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read, a partition is an ordinary wall. To copy a floor with its content, use duplicate_level.

buildingId.description: The building. Default: the building of the floor the person is viewing, else the scene's only building.

position.description: above (default): over the top storey, under the roof level; below: under the lowest, a basement.

height.description: Floor-to-floor storey height (default 2.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

tools.name: create_stair
tools.title: Create stair
tools.description:
Create a staircase rising from a level, as the editor's stair tool builds one: straight, L (a flight, a landing as deep as the stair is wide, a flight turned 90°) or U (a flight, a landing across, a flight back beside the first). It rises to the level above and owns the floor opening it cuts in every floor it passes; when no level stands above, a blank one is made for it. toLevelId null makes a flight to no level (porch steps, a deck, a raised platform): it rises height, cuts nothing and makes no level. Refused with a code: a flight to or from a declared roof level, and a toLevelId that is not above the level it rises from.

GEOMETRY (get this wrong and the stair pokes through a wall):
- (x, z) is the middle of the bottom riser, where the flight starts. The first flight runs from there along the climb: at rotation 0 it covers x − width/2 .. x + width/2 and z .. z + its run.
- rotation in degrees about Y: 0 climbs toward +Z, 90 → +X, 180 → −Z, 270 → −X. Point the climb into the room, away from the wall the bottom step sits against.
- An L or U turns to the climber's left or right (turn). The result gives the whole footprint and the point the top step arrives at.
- Keep 0.9 m clear at the foot and at the head of the flight, and the whole footprint inside one room on both levels (a hall is typical): read the room's outline first (get_zones).

OPENINGS: by default the stair owns the opening over its flights and keeps it as the stair moves (openingOffset widens it). An opening of another size, centre or turn, through a slab or ceiling you name, or through one of the two only, is cut as an opening the stair owns, as given.

x.description: X of the middle of the bottom riser.

z.description: Z of the middle of the bottom riser.

rotation.description: The first flight's climb (default 0 = toward +Z; 90 = +X, 180 = −Z, 270 = −X). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

layout.description: straight (default); l: a flight, a landing, a flight turned 90°; u: a flight, a landing across, a flight back beside the first.

turn.description: Which way an L or U turns, to the climber's left or right (default left).

lowerSteps.description: An L or U's risers in the first flight; the rest are in the last (default half).

width.description: Side-to-side width, across the climb (default 1.0 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

length.description: The flights' horizontal run along the climb, landings aside (default: from the stair's design targets, 0.28 m of going per riser, risers of at most 0.18 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Vertical rise. Omit it unless asked for a specific rise: the flight then follows the storey's floor-to-floor height and keeps tracking it. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

steps.description: Number of risers in all. Omit it to derive ~18 cm risers from the rise; pass it when the run was planned from a step count.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

toLevelId.description: The level the flight arrives on. Default: the next level above, created when there is none. null: a flight to no level, rising height (default the storey's floor-to-floor height).

railingMode.description: Which sides have a railing, looking up the flight (default both).

railingStyle.description: How the railings are built (default balusters): post-and-rail, cable (contemporary with a black railingMaterial), boards, glass or metal.

railingMaterial.description: A library material for the railings (library:<id>); an unknown one is refused.

materialPreset.description: A library material for the flight (library:<id>); an unknown one is refused.

createDestinationSlabOpening.description: Cut the floor it arrives through (default true).

createSourceCeilingOpening.description: Cut the ceiling of the floor it leaves (default true).

destinationSlabId.description: The slab it arrives through. Default: the floor of the level it arrives on.

sourceCeilingId.description: The ceiling it rises through. Default: the ceiling of the level it leaves.

openingWidth.description: The opening across the climb (default the stair's footprint). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

openingLength.description: The opening along the climb (default the stair's footprint). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

openingOffset.description: A margin round the opening on every side (default 0.08 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

openingCenter.description: The opening centre (x, z). Default: the middle of the stair's footprint.

openingRotation.description: The opening's turn (default the stair's). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

tools.name: create_roof
tools.title: Create roof
tools.description: Cap a storey with a roof over its footprint (its walls' outline, else its floor plates, else its rooms), swept in the building's own axes into rectangles, one roof segment each. Without a roofType: a gable for one rectangle, hips for a few wings, flat for a large block. The roof goes on the building's roof level above the top storey (the empty level directly above when it is the only one; made, named Roof, when there is none), and stands on the storey's wall tops, so exploded and solo level views lift it off the plan. Glazed construction supports gable, straight shed and barrel. Barrel depth is the span; barrelRise is at most half the span. glazing controls frame, glass, grids and panels. Paint glazing-frame, glazing-glass or glazing-solid. Call it once the storeys and their exterior walls stand. Refused with a code: storey_above (another storey stands above: a roof caps the top one; a lower wing's roof is drawn with the Roof tool), building_required (no level named on a site of several buildings: pass a level of the one to roof), roof_exists (the storey already has a roof: edit it, or delete_node it first when the person asked for a new one), no_rooms (no rooms or closed walls on any level of the building: pass width and depth to roof a rectangle of your own).

spacing.description: Bar spacing, for the maximum-spacing and fixed-spacing layouts. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Range 0.2–100 m.
Bar spacing, for the maximum-spacing and fixed-spacing layouts. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Range 0.2–100 m.

frameWidth.description: Frame bar width. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

frameDepth.description: Frame bar depth. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

glassThickness.description: Glass pane thickness. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

barrelRise.description: Barrel arch rise, at most half each segment span. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

wallThickness.description: Roof wall thickness. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

levelId.description: The storey to cover, by an id list_levels returned. Default: the top storey with rooms. A level without rooms stands for the highest storey of its building that has some.

roofType.description: The shape of every segment. Default: chosen from the footprint.

pitch.description: Slope of the roof planes (default 40°). In degrees, or rise over run ("6:12"). Range 0–85 deg.

overhang.description: Eave overhang: how far the eaves reach past the walls in plan (a segment stores it along its slope). Read it from the photo: a deep modern overhang is 1–2 m. Default 0.3. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

wallHeight.description: Knee walls under the eaves (default 0: the roof starts at the wall tops). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

width.description: With depth: roof a rectangle of your own instead of the footprint (a wing, or walls drawn without rooms), along x. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

depth.description: The rectangle's depth, along z. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

center.description: The rectangle's centre [x, z] in metres (default [0, 0]).

materialPreset.description: The roof finish, a library material.

fasciaHeight.description: A fascia band of that height round the roof's eaves and rakes; on a flat roof it reaches the roof's top, a coping over its edge. Absent (and no fasciaMaterialPreset): no band. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

fasciaMaterialPreset.description: The band's finish, a library material (a black fascia: library:preset-nearblack); the roof's wall finish when absent.

name.description: What the user would call it (default "Roof").

tools.name: move_roofs_to_roof_level
tools.title: Move roofs to the roof level
tools.description: Move the roofs a storey holds on its own walls to the level the roof rule gives them, as a roof's panel does by hand (Move to the roof level): over the top storey, the building's roof level (made, named Roof, when there is none); under an upper storey, that storey. Each roof stands exactly where it stood, its segments, finishes and id kept: only the level holding it changes, so exploded and solo level views show the storey's plan with no roof over it. For a project built before roofs had their own level, when verify_scene reports roof_mixed_in_storey. Refused with a code: level_not_found, no_roof_on_walls (the storey holds no roof standing on its walls; a porch roof on its beam and a lower wing's roof on the storey above already sit where they belong). Returns the roofs moved (roofIds), the level they went to (roofLevelId) and the roof level made for them (createdRoofLevelId).

levelId.description: The storey whose roofs move, by an id list_levels returned.

tools.name: place_items
tools.title: Place items
tools.description: Place one or more catalog items (furniture, fixtures, plants, art, lights) in one call. Each assetId is a known catalog id, available from search_assets results or existing scene item data, never guessed. Positions are level (x, z) metres. An item stands on the floor of the level, or on the host it names (targetNodeId): a wall (art, a sconce: y is the height of its bottom above the floor, required; it goes on the side of the wall the point is on), a ceiling (a pendant, a downlight: it hangs flush under it), or an item standing on the floor (a lamp on a nightstand: it rests on its top; on an object built with add_object it rests on the real surface under the point, such as a porch landing, or a ceiling item hangs from the underside above it, such as a sloped vault, and the result names it in restingOn). A room, a slab or a level as the target means its floor. Each item is placed or refused on its own (asset_not_found; outside_rooms: an indoor item on the floor outside every room of a level that has rooms — garden and outdoor items may stand outside; height_required, item_too_tall, unsupported_host, host_not_found, host_not_on_level; blocks_door: a floor item standing where a door needs space, with a spot in its room that clears every door; too_large_for_room: a floor item its room cannot hold in any turn).

assetId.description: A known catalog id; search_assets can find it.

y.description: Height above the floor (metres): on a wall, of the item's bottom (required: art centred at eye level is 1.5 − its height / 2, a sconce about 1.5); on an item, a resting height you set rather than its top. Not used on a floor or a ceiling.

targetNodeId.description: The host: a wall, a ceiling or an item standing on the floor; a room, a slab or a level means its floor. Default: the level's floor.

rotation.description: Turn about the vertical (default 0). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

tools.name: delete_node
tools.title: Delete node
tools.description: Delete a node with everything under it, as the editor's Delete does: a wall goes with its doors and windows, a level with everything on it. The floors above a deleted level keep their index.

tools.name: create_room
tools.title: Create room
tools.description: Create a room on a level from its polygon: a wall per edge, an edge a wall already runs along reusing that wall (rooms share their boundary with their neighbour), and the room zone that names it. The floor plate and the ceiling are derived from the room — never author a slab or a ceiling for it. Declare the room's doors and windows in the same call by polygon edge (wallIndex) and t along it, no wall ids needed; each is placed with add_door's and add_window's rules, and one that cannot be is skipped and listed in skippedOpenings with its code. Returns zoneId, slabId, ceilingId, wallIds in edge order (null where no wall), doorIds, windowIds. outdoor: true draws a terrace instead: separators where no wall runs, no walls of its own and no ceiling. Where the walls already enclose a room the reconciler numbered, the call names that room instead of adding a second one; where they enclose a room with a name of its own (not a number the editor gave it), it is refused (room_named_by_person) unless rename is true, which you pass only when the person asked for the rename, so a name is never changed silently.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

polygon.description: The corners in order, as [x, z] in metres.

color.description: Hex colour of the room zone, e.g. "#22c55e"; omit it and the room gets a palette colour picked from its id.

wallHeight.description: Omit to follow the storey and covering-slab underside. Equal to the stored storey height also follows that plane; other values are body heights above the wall's support, including deliberately taller walls. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

wallThickness.description: Thickness of the walls it builds. Omitted, a wall against the ground on a level below grade is a foundation wall built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read, a partition inside the outline is an ordinary wall; a thickness keeps the schema wall. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rename.description: Only where the walls already enclose a room with a name of its own (not a number the editor gave it): true names that room with `name` instead of the refusal room_named_by_person. Pass it only when the person asked for the rename; otherwise ask them first.

outdoor.description: true for an outdoor room (a terrace): closed with separators (the editor's Separator: a room boundary with no wall) where no wall runs, no walls of its own and no ceiling.

doors.description: The entry door and the doors to the rooms next to it.

wallIndex.description: The polygon edge it sits on: edge i runs from corner i to corner i + 1.

t.description: Position along that edge: 0 = its start, 1 = its end (default 0.5).

width.description: Door width (default 0.9 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Door height (default 2.1 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

swingDirection.description: Which way the door opens (default inward).

style.description: Visual preset: 'panel' (default raised-panel), 'glass' (mostly glass), 'modern' (flush slab), 'paneled-glass' (glass top, panel bottom — an entry door), 'french' (two narrow glass leaves), 'shaker' (one flat panel), 'six-panel' (3 × 2 traditional grid), 'craftsman' (4 stacked vertical panels), 'half-louvered' (slats on top, panel below — closet, laundry), 'barn' (wide recessed panel). One style per room type across the home; the entry door may differ.

windows.description: Windows, on exterior edges only: not on an edge shared with another room.

wallIndex.description: The polygon edge it sits on: edge i runs from corner i to corner i + 1.

t.description: Position along that edge: 0 = its start, 1 = its end (default 0.5).

width.description: Window width (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Window height (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillHeight.description: Height from the floor to the bottom of the window (default: centred vertically on the wall). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

style.description: Visual preset: 'single' (default single pane), 'double-hung', 'triple-hung' (stacked sashes), 'casement' (two panes side by side), 'sliding' (three side by side — wide), 'grid' (2 × 2), 'tall-grid' (2 × 3), 'wide-grid' (3 × 2), 'horizontal-bands' (4 stacked bands), 'transom' (a small row over a larger pane), 'picture' (an alias of 'single'). One style for all the windows of a room, and per room type across the home.

tools.name: furnish_room
tools.title: Furnish room
tools.description: Place the catalog's fixed furniture set for a room type: one set per type, not matched to a style. The bed, sofa, counters or toilet go against the wall facing the door, the rest along a side wall, each set off its wall by its own depth. Name the room by zoneId (its level and outline come with it), or give its polygon and level. The door wall is the edge a door of the room stands on, else doorWallIndex, else edge 0. Nothing lands in a door's clear zone or on another item: a piece that does not fit is nudged, else skipped, and skipped says why. Items stand on the room's level. The set per room type: bedroom: double-bed (a side of 3.2 m or more) or single-bed, two bedside-table, dresser (10 m² or more), closet (13 m² or more); kitchen: kitchen (back wall of 2.6 m or more) or kitchen-counter, stove (back wall of 3.5 m or more), fridge; bathroom: toilet, bathroom-sink, bathtub (6.5 m² or more) or shower-square; living: sofa, coffee-table, livingroom-chair, tv-stand; dining: dining-table, two dining-chair (four when both sides are 3 m or more); laundry: washing-machine, drying-rack; entry and hallway: coat-rack (both sides 1.4 m or more); storage: closet. The result lists each piece placed with its size and id, and each piece skipped with its reason. view_scene with interior { zoneId } shows the room from inside, at a person's height.

zoneId.description: The room: zoneId from create_room, or an id from get_zones.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

polygon.description: The room's corners as [x, z] in metres, when there is no zoneId.

doorWallIndex.description: The polygon edge (i → i + 1) to treat as the door wall: for a room with no door yet, or to override the one found.

tools.name: paint
tools.title: Paint
tools.description: Give walls, slabs, ceilings, roofs, columns, fences, doors, windows, stairs, blocks, cabinets, shelves, items and the other built parts a finish in one call, as the editor's Paint does. Give one finish: color (#rrggbb, painted with the nearest of the library's flat colours, said with how near); material, a library:<id> (find it with search_materials) or scene:<id> ref, or a native material {properties: {color, roughness, metalness}} for an exact finish, kept as a scene material (materialName names a new one) and reused when the scene holds an equal one; or erase: true, back to the surface's default. role picks the surface: a wall's face a or b, or exterior and interior (the faces turned out of its rooms or into them, else by its stored sides; a partition is interior on both; a wall whose sides are unknown, or with rooms along only part of a face, is refused: name its face, a or b), its trims aSkirting, bSkirting, aCrown, bCrown, aChairRail, bChairRail (skirting, crown or chairRail: that trim on both faces), a curtain wall's curtain-frame, curtain-glass, curtain-solid; a slab's surface, side, edge, riser, underside or foundation; a ceiling's surface; a roof's top (the covering), edge (the gable ends and the trim band), wall (the soffit and the deck edge, and the fascia and rake boards unless they have their own) or fascia (the fascia and rake boards, a fascia band); a glazed roof's glazing-frame, glazing-glass or glazing-solid; a column's shaft, base, capital or frame; a fence's posts, infill, base or rail; a door's panel, frame, glass or hardware; a window's frame or glass; a stair's treads, body or railing; a block's body; a cabinet's front, carcass, countertop, plinth, hardware or glass; another part's own slots, which a refusal names; an item's surfaces by the names its model gives them (its painted ones are in get_node's slots), which paint cannot check. Without a role: both faces of a wall, a slab's or a ceiling's surface, a roof's top, a glazed roof's frame and solid panels, a column's shaft, a whole fence, a door's panel and frame, a window's frame, a block's body, a part's one surface. A roof shows one finish per surface: a segment's finish goes on its roof, and a roof's on all of its segments. A glazed segment holds its own glazing finishes: a roof's glazing roles go on its glazed segments, its other roles on the roof, and without a role both. A wall face is painted whole, over the wall finish of the room it faces; its painted parts keep their own, named in the note. A ceiling shows its finish's colour, not its texture. The result says the finish written, and the scene material when there is one. A target that is not in the scene, a role it lacks or an unknown material refuses the whole call: nothing is painted.

color.description: A colour, #rrggbb: painted with the nearest library colour.

material.description: A library:<id> or scene:<id> ref, or a native material (properties color, roughness, metalness, and an existing texture) kept as a scene material.

materialName.description: The name of a new native material; an equal one already in the scene keeps its own.

tools.name: place_in_room
tools.title: Place an item in a room
tools.description: Put one floor-standing catalog item in a room where it fits, without working out a position. Wall/ceiling-attached assets need a host: place_items accepts targetNodeId and, for a wall, y for the bottom height. A wall-bound floor piece (fridge, counter, stove, sink, TV stand, dresser, wardrobe, sofa, bed, bedside table, toilet, bath, shower, bookcase, cabinet) stands against a wall, centred in the widest free stretch of that wall (clear of every door and every other item), its front toward the room; it is never put in the middle, and when no wall has room the answer says how wide the widest free stretch is. A free-standing piece (dining table, rug, coffee table, plant, armchair) takes the middle of the room, or goes with what it belongs with: a coffee table and an armchair face the sofa. A chair goes around its table, one call per chair, facing the table, and is refused when the room has no table. Explicit edge, align, offset or inset instead requests a wall free run for any floor piece. Name the room by its zoneId (create_room, get_zones), or by its polygon and level. The item is a catalog id from search_assets. To furnish a whole room by its type in one call, use furnish_room.

assetId.description: A known catalog id; search_assets can find it.

zoneId.description: The room: zoneId from create_room, or an id from get_zones.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

polygon.description: The room's corners as [x, z] in metres, when there is no zoneId.

edge.description: Stand it against this polygon edge (i → i + 1) instead of the best one.

rotationDeg.description: World yaw in degrees, overriding the automatic inward, group or table-facing yaw. In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

facing.description: In by default. Out adds 180 degrees after any explicit rotationDeg.

align.description: Desired wall alignment, clamped into a valid free run. Defaults to the widest run’s center.

offset.description: Signed metres along the wall from the desired alignment; defaults to zero. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

inset.description: Normal gap in metres between the rotated footprint and the wall centerline; defaults to 0.1 m. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

clearanceAreas.description: Existing clearance rectangles, in world metres, to keep free before placing.

allowDuplicate.description: Place it even though the room already has this item. Off by default (a second toilet or stove is a mistake); chairs are always allowed.

tools.name: get_site
tools.title: Get site
tools.description: Read the site a building stands on, in its level coordinates: the lot and its area, with the footprint a house usually covers on it (30 to 45%); the buildable area inside the setbacks with its centre, its area, each edge's frontage and depth, and its front edge (behind the street; while no street is recorded, behind the edge facing north, which the setbacks take as the front); the street side with the lot's frontage and depth on it; north; the ground (sloped with its fall, read flat, or not read); the address, parcel and zoning when known; whether the lot is only the new-project placeholder; and where the footprint sits now with its yards.

building.description: The building, by its id (list_levels' parentId). Default: the building of the floor the person is viewing, else the scene's only building.

site.description: The site, by its id (get_site's siteId), when the scene has several: a lot no building stands on yet reads in site coordinates. Default: the building's site.

tools.name: place_building
tools.title: Place building
tools.description: Stand a building on its site before or after its walls go up. It moves only the building node, so walls, levels and roofs keep their coordinates and move with it. The footprint (outline, the plan you are about to draw, in the coordinates you will draw it; else the walls standing) lands centred in the buildable area, or at the yards a site plan or the person gives. A building with walls keeps its rotation unless rotationDeg is given (get_site's squareRotationDeg squares it to the street); one with none yet is turned square to the street. Fences, paths and plants on its levels move with it.

building.description: The building, by its id (list_levels' parentId). Default: the building of the floor the person is viewing, else the scene's only building.

outline.description: The footprint's corners in order, as [x, z] in metres, in the level coordinates the walls are (or will be) drawn in. Default: the walls standing.

right.description: The right (seen from the street) yard: from the lot line to the house, square to the house. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.
